title: Finite constant extensions inside an algebraically closed overfield
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field, let $k$ be an algebraically closed extension field of $k_0$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $m$ be a nonzero natural number. Then there exists an intermediate field $K$ with $k_0\subseteq K\subseteq k$ such that $K$ is finite and $\#K=(\#k_0)^m$. This is only the existence assertion; no root-set or uniqueness assertion is needed.

source.place: Paragraph 1, finite constant extension; proved source implementation WeilConjectures.TraceFormula.ModelExtension, lines 48--59.

proof.text: Take the finite field Extension k0 (ringChar k0) m from Mathlib. Embed it as a k0-algebra into the algebraically closed overfield k. Its field range is an intermediate field K, and the induced algebra equivalence proves that K is finite. Transport Nat.card across this equivalence and apply FiniteField.natCard_extension to obtain the required cardinality. This is the complete existing Lean proof of ProEtale.CondensedRing.exists_intermediateField_natCard_eq_pow; no new theorem is being assumed.
